newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firm in brief pre-Christmas rally.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firm in brief pre-Christmas rally.

text.p: Croatian stocks, bolstered by pharmaceutical firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, firmed on Tuesday but a surprise pre-Christmas rally was seen as short-lived.
All four active issues, including food concern Podravka and Kras chocolate maker, notched up a few percentage points ahead of a two-day bourse closure.
Turnover hit a decent 14.3 million kuna as investors returned to Zagreb briefly to cash in on the rise of Pliva and Zagrebacka GDRs in London to $53.62-$54 and $20.56/78 respectively.
But traders suspected their interest would not spill over into other issues, inciting a bull run of the last autumn's proportions, before well into next spring.
"I expect stagnation to last through January," said Velimir Zelimorski of brokerage Fima.
Zagrebacka was the biggest gainer, closing 4.90 percent up at 1,070 kuna, 20 down from the intraday high. It was also the most actively traded issue with 2,506 units sold.
Pliva rose 2.94 percent to 14,000 kuna on volume of 819.

Podravka gained five kuna after mixed trade to end at 215 kuna on volume of 724 shares. Its stock is expected to rise steadily from present low levels as the company presses on with financial consolidation.
"Podravka has a big potential to strengthen when it sells loss-making subsidiaries," said Zelimorski. "It still has some aces up its sleeve."
Kras added a modest 2.20 percent or nine kuna to 419, selling only 221 shares.
The Zagreb bourse will reopen for trade on Friday.
